records.title: Make document quality review evidence-backed
records.summary: Use the Site for reusable methods and a source-grounded brief for each application. Treat integrity, chronology, and extraction as prerequisites to judging reader and document quality.
records.question: How should document quality be reviewed without mistaking cosmetic polish or approval labels for evidence?
records.decision: Expand the existing editorial Skills, reconcile Leah and Sofia, use a small content trial, and require version-specific independent findings before a review can pass.
records.rationale: A resume audit found changed attribution and action verbs, weakened context, cosmetic variations, and approval labels without inspectable review evidence. The process is adopted; its effect on the next resume remains untested.
records.alternatives: Another full visual redesign; a universal resume score; additional Personas; an app-managed runtime. Start with existing capabilities and a bounded trial.
records.tradeoffs: Claim tracking and concrete findings take more care. Focus them on consequential claims and affected checks; do not add a general approval ritual to every edit.
records.affects: Skills, Leah, Sofia, job-search handoffs, Docs, and the isolated resume editorial trial.
records.revisit: A real trial still produces generic or misleading content, the reviewer cannot find evidence, or the process creates effort without improving the reader’s understanding.

records.title: Flow hierarchy for Persona work
records.summary: Organize each person’s work into foundational, supporting, and edge-case flows, with the activity inventory embedded inside each flow.
records.question: Should the Persona page follow a day, a list of activities, or the outcomes the person is trying to produce?
records.decision: Use flow hierarchy as the primary structure. Each tier can contain multiple workflows.
records.rationale: This keeps cadence, tools, priorities, friction, and recovery work attached to the context where they matter.
records.affects: Persona cards, Persona detail views, and the persona-research guidance.
records.evidence: Layout Lab prototype and current Docs guidance.
records.revisit: Real Persona research shows that users need a different first-order way to compare work.

records.title: Skill index plus deep dive
records.summary: Keep the complete capability set visible, then select one Skill to inspect its triggers, operating model, quality signals, workflows, and evidence.
records.question: Can someone see all the capabilities and still understand one Skill deeply?
records.decision: Use a scan-friendly Skill index with a focused deep-dive panel.
records.rationale: The index supports orientation; depth belongs in the selected Skill instead of a wall of content.
records.affects: Persona detail pages, the Skills space, and persona-skills guidance.
records.evidence: Skill Layout Lab prototype and current Docs guidance.
records.revisit: Skill reuse or relationship density makes the index difficult to scan or the panel too shallow.

records.title: Full Skill network map
records.summary: Show multi-hop relationships between primitive capabilities, composed Skills, workflows, and Personas.
records.decision: Park until the focused Skill map needs a global relationship view.
records.rationale: A global graph needs filtering, navigation, and accessible list-view rules before it becomes useful.
records.affects: Future Skills navigation and relationship views.
records.revisit: A global relationship view becomes necessary for real reuse and remains usable with filtering and accessible alternatives.

records.title: Skill composition editor
records.summary: Let a maintainer assemble composed Skills from existing primitives and connect them with typed relationships.
records.decision: Park until relationship editing has stronger validation, permissions, and versioning.
records.rationale: Editing shared relationships safely has a larger integrity and governance surface than the static library needs today.
records.affects: Future Skill authoring and relationship editing.
records.revisit: Start with reuse suggestions, duplicate and cycle checks, and an explicit rationale for every new connection.

records.title: Skill coverage and assessment
records.summary: Show which Skills are well evidenced, thinly evidenced, or missing across Personas and workflows.
records.decision: Park until more Personas and Skill applications have been researched consistently.
records.rationale: Coverage metrics would create false precision before the evidence model is mature enough.
records.revisit: Potential views include evidence confidence, workflow coverage, proficiency signals, and validation gaps.

records.title: Dependency-aware version history
records.summary: Show what downstream Personas, workflows, and composed Skills are affected when a reusable capability changes.
records.decision: Park until the relationship graph has enough real reuse to create meaningful change impact.
records.rationale: Impact views are most useful when a change can affect several real dependents.
records.affects: Future relationship diffs and reconciliation prompts.
records.revisit: Pair relationship diffs with reconciliation prompts and a review queue before changes propagate.

records.title: Operating Packs are contextual library space
records.summary: Catalog reusable, file-based operating context alongside the existing library spaces while keeping actual Markdown source outside the catalog when appropriate.
records.question: Where should domain or project instructions, standards, conventions, procedures, references, and validation guidance live when they are reusable but not executable capabilities?
records.decision: Add Operating Packs as a first-class space with a small source/location record, explicit availability, and scoped Persona, Skill, workflow, Playbook, and Tool-use relationships.
records.rationale: Contextual rules need a durable home that does not turn Skills into project instruction or Playbooks into duplicated policy. Scoped applications keep a pack relevant to the work where it applies.
records.tradeoffs: The catalog does not transport or execute packs, and external references may remain planned or unavailable until verified. Project conventions remain local unless later evidence supports broader reuse.
records.affects: Orientation routing, Docs, Site navigation, the Operating Pack catalog, lifecycle Skills, and reconciliation guidance.
records.revisit: A pack needs executable runtime behavior, repeated rules reveal a generalizable Skill, a Playbook duplicates pack content, or external source transport becomes a separately authorized product need.

records.title: Templates are reusable starting artifacts
records.summary: Add Templates as a first-class library space beside Operating Packs while preserving a distinct ownership boundary for reusable starting structure.
records.question: Where should reusable starting structures and scaffolds live when they accelerate work but do not define how the work should be performed?
records.decision: Catalog Template identity, purpose, applicability, source metadata, evidence, lifecycle, revision context, and relationships in Persona-Library. Keep actual reusable artifacts in their canonical external or project source.
records.rationale: Templates answer what to start from. Operating Packs answer how to work within context; Skills own reusable judgment; Tools own execution and permissions; Playbooks own coordination and outcomes.
records.tradeoffs: The static catalog can describe a planned external artifact without making it available. The system does not fetch, clone, render, execute, publish, or upgrade Template artifacts yet.
records.affects: Orientation routing, Template normalization, lifecycle Skills, validation, Docs, Site navigation, generated data, and reconciliation guidance.
records.evidence: Templates catalog, Docs boundary, and inspected template-library main revision f88a4011902b58b2f192305f5a731f1a71263965.
records.revisit: External Template paths become real, a project starter demonstrates broader reuse, Template relationships need new dimensions, or artifact transport/execution becomes separately authorized.

records.title: Template Librarian stewards the collection
records.summary: Add a library-stewardship Persona for Template discoverability, provenance, lifecycle, and routing while keeping substantive Template quality with domain specialists.
records.question: Who keeps the Template collection organized and trustworthy without becoming the domain expert for every artifact?
records.decision: Use the Template Librarian to maintain catalog identity, source verification, duplication control, promotion, deprecation, relocation, and reconciliation. Route discipline-specific research and composition to the relevant specialist.
records.rationale: Library stewardship and domain judgment are different kinds of work. Keeping them separate preserves the Template boundary and lets the collection grow without turning one Persona into a polymath.
records.affects: Template routing, Persona workflows and handoffs, Template lifecycle Skills, Docs, generated Persona output, and reconciliation. Mara Okoye remains the escalation point for architecture and concept-boundary questions.
records.evidence: Template Librarian Persona, Templates catalog, Templates guidance, and issue #63.
records.revisit: Observed Template work shows that stewardship and domain composition cannot remain separate, a dedicated reusable capability is justified, or external artifact ownership changes.

records.title: Bounded parallel implementation is a distinct Playbook
records.summary: Keep Multi-Persona Collaboration as named-Persona synthesis through a shared problem-context. Catalog bounded parallel repository implementation as its own Playbook with Coordinator, Implementer, Reviewer, and Authorizer roles.
records.question: Should usage-conscious parallel implementation be a new Playbook or a profile of Multi-Persona Collaboration?
records.decision: Add playbook-bounded-parallel-implementation as a distinct Playbook. Reference collaboration instead of copying its stages, solution-quality gate, or problem-context contract. Do not create an Agent, Coordinator, Runtime, Budget, or Scheduler entity.
records.rationale: Collaboration produces one inspectable solution from Persona lenses. Bounded parallel implementation produces independent reviewable PRs with one-level delegation, compact handoffs, independent review, and separately authorized merge.
records.alternatives: Extend Multi-Persona Collaboration; wait for #71; encode ChatGPT Work or Codex as canonical meaning. Rejected because those options mix synthesis with mutation gates or bind the contract to a runtime.
records.affects: Playbook catalog, Playbooks orientation route, Site Playbooks and Docs surfaces, root activation, and Work Order evidence for #82, #86, #89, and #94.
records.evidence: Issues #71, #82, #86, #89, and #94 plus the bounded-parallel Work Order.
records.revisit: A two-repository proof is needed, or runtime-specific procedure becomes substantial enough for a Tool package.

records.status_note: The front-door conclusion is qualified by DEC-013; the remaining role and privacy boundaries remain applied.
records.title: Riley orchestrates job search; the Playbook owns the outcome
records.summary: Keep Riley Morgan’s identity as AI orchestrator. Evidence-led Job Search remains the reusable outcome Playbook. Specialists own domain judgment. Do not create a generic Job Search Persona or store private job history in Persona-Library.
records.question: Should Riley Morgan become the domain-owning Job Search Persona, or remain a reusable orchestrator for the Evidence-led Job Search Playbook?
records.decision: Playbook owns the outcome. Riley Morgan coordinates contributors. Elena, Marcus, Leah, Samira, Camille, and Sofia retain specialist ownership. Private opportunity history uses the job ledger contract in candidate workspace state. No new Job Search Persona.
records.rationale: Collapsing job-search expertise into Riley would make the reusable AI orchestrator identity accumulate domain methods and blur specialist quality criteria. The valid boundary is to keep search strategy, hiring calibration, narrative, outreach, visual, and document judgment with existing specialists.
records.alternatives: Create a new Job Search Persona; rename Riley to Job Search Orchestrator; leave job-search orchestrator labels as-is. Rejected because no uncovered responsibility justified a new Persona and identity drift would damage reuse.
records.affects: Job-search guidance, Playbooks and job-search Site surfaces, the Docs resume-application-work route, job-ledger contract, and issue #90 evidence. Riley’s canonical roleLabel remains AI orchestrator.
records.evidence: Issue #90 ownership correction and the job-ledger contract.
records.revisit: Implementation evidence shows a real uncovered job-search responsibility not owned by the existing specialists, Riley, or the Playbook; or a callable job-search Skill is authorized beyond the ledger contract.

records.title: Template lifecycle is a distinct Playbook
records.summary: Catalog playbook-template-lifecycle as the reusable coordination model for researching, composing, promoting, maintaining, and reconciling Templates.
records.question: Should the Template lifecycle remain only a sequence of Skills and Librarian workflows, or become a canonical Playbook?
records.decision: Add playbook-template-lifecycle. Reference existing Template Librarian workflows, Template Skills, domain specialists, DEC-008/009, and external template-library ownership instead of copying them. Do not create a new Persona, Skill, registry, or runtime.
records.rationale: The Template system crosses stewardship, domain quality, external artifact ownership, promotion evidence, and reconciliation. That repeated cross-owner outcome needs an inspectable stage and gate contract without making every bounded Skill action a mandatory Playbook run.
records.alternatives: Leave the outcome undocumented; fold it into Skill formation; invent a Template runtime or registry. Rejected because the owners and gates are distinct from Skill formation or execution infrastructure.
records.affects: Playbook catalog, Playbooks orientation route, Templates stewardship handoff, Site Playbooks/Docs/Decisions surfaces, and issue #72 evidence.
records.evidence: Template lifecycle Work Order, catalog, route, and Docs example.
records.revisit: Repeated runs show a missing stage or gate, a callable Template package is authorized, or bounded Skill actions prove the Playbook is unnecessary overhead.

records.title: Riley is the default routing front door
records.summary: Riley Morgan is the default interaction and routing front door for unqualified requests while Playbooks retain procedural ownership and specialists retain domain judgment.
records.question: How should an unqualified request enter the Persona Library when the work may be narrow specialist work or a larger reusable outcome?
records.decision: Riley interprets intent and selects the smallest useful route: narrow work may go to a specialist or Skill; outcome-scale work may go to a Playbook; a bounded consultation, Tool path, or other focused route may be selected when that is the smallest useful fit. Explicit requests naming a specialist, Skill, or Playbook may route directly without an artificial Riley hop.
records.rationale: Issue #90 correctly removed job-search domain ownership from Riley, but its front-door wording also made the Evidence-led Job Search Playbook appear to be the default entry. Separating entry/routing ownership from procedural and domain ownership restores the intended interaction model without adding a runtime router or moving expertise.
records.alternatives: Keep the Playbook as the universal front door; make Riley own the complete job-search method; add a routing service or registry. Rejected because these options either force taxonomy-first interaction, transfer specialist judgment, or add unnecessary runtime architecture.
records.tradeoffs: Riley must choose among routes without absorbing their expertise. The route contract needs explicit tests and should be revisited if observed requests consistently choose a larger or less capable path than the smallest useful route.
records.affects: docs/job-search/implementation.md; content/orientation/docs.json; Riley’s authored record and maintenance history; routing validators/tests; generated library and Decisions output; issue #111.
records.evidence: Issue #111, PR #112, the Riley Persona/workflow sources, the four explicit routing tests, and Mara’s placement review recorded in the issue-111 Work Order.
records.revisit: Observed requests show that Riley’s route selection consistently chooses a larger or less capable path than the smallest useful route, or a later Decision establishes a different universal entry contract.
